meta.title: Fix Gradle build failures due to Maven Central rate limiting (HTTP 429)
meta.body_summary: Add Gradle dependency caching to all Java CI workflows to resolve Maven Central HTTP 429 rate limiting and reduce build times by avoiding repeated downloads.

perf_labels.notes: Copilot added Gradle caching to CI workflows to fix Maven Central 429 errors; two maintainers approved without comment after ~1.8h, merged.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 85 changed lines across 3 CI workflow files, this is a small edit by absolute volume. It fits a small-step, fast-turnaround CI fix PR and is consistent with the successful, low-friction merge.

review_details.performance_claim: Reduce CI build time and mitigate Maven Central HTTP 429 rate limiting by caching Gradle dependencies (~200MB no longer downloaded every run).

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: CI workflow caching configuration is straightforward for Copilot; the agent can modify YAML-based CI files and understand caching patterns. Merge required no review commentary, indicating low complexity.

detection_detail.ci_auto: The original problem (HTTP 429 rate limiting) was detected by CI failing jobs; the fix is expected to resolve these failures, and maintainers presumably monitored CI after merge.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark or explicit reproduction steps; the PR relies on reasoning that caching will reduce downloads, and no performance measurement was requested.

core_change_summary.description: Added Gradle dependency caching to three CI workflow files (java.yml, codeql.yml, java-cd.yml) using actions/cache with keys based on gradle file hashes, and added --build-cache to gradlew commands.
change_trajectory: Single substantive commit adding caching steps to all three workflow YAML files.
No further commits; two approvals and merge within ~1.8 hours.

Second APPROVED review with no body text.

collaboration_trajectory: Copilot opened PR linked to issue, added caching configuration in a single commit.
Two maintainers approved without comment within ~1.8 hours.
PR merged immediately after second approval.
